reason: The star is central to both goals, so checking its available partners should clarify how to begin building its interior.
expectation: The inspection should reveal which available ingredients can advance the star's evolution.

choice.with: Hydrogen nuclei in the stellar core

alternatives.reason: Hydrogen fusion powers the star, but the next stage is not yet clear.

effect: Hydrogen fusion produced a helium-rich core, suggesting the next stage involves changes within that core.
reaction: The distinction between the core and a separate object was useful.
reason: Compression in the stellar core plausibly advances the helium-rich core toward its next fusion stage.
expectation: The core should contract and heat, preparing it for helium fusion.

effect: Compression raised the core's temperature enough to begin helium burning.
reaction: The distinction between nuclear burning and ordinary chemical heat is useful.
reason: Neutral helium is the visible material most plausibly associated with the core's new burning stage.
expectation: Helium burning should produce heavier material in the core.

effect: Helium burning produced carbon-rich stellar material through the triple-alpha process.
reaction: The unstable intermediate makes carbon production more interesting than a simple three-way collision.
reason: Further compression may heat the carbon-rich material enough for the next fusion stage.
expectation: Compression should advance the core toward carbon burning.

effect: Compression advanced the carbon-rich material to carbon-burning layers, producing several heavier elements.
reaction: The multiple reaction channels were a useful detail.
reason: Further compression may raise the temperature enough to advance the burning layers toward the layered interior.
expectation: The layers should progress to a hotter stage of stellar burning.

effect: Compression advanced the layers through neon and oxygen burning, producing elements including silicon and sulfur.
reaction: The continuing burning shells clarify how the layered interior develops.
reason: Further compression has advanced the previous burning stages and may lead to silicon burning.
expectation: The layers should advance to a hotter burning stage.

effect: Compression produced silicon-burning material and was consumed; reactions in this stage move nuclei toward the iron group.
reaction: The distinction between a reaction network and a single silicon collision was useful.
reason: Compression is no longer available, so inspecting the silicon-burning material should reveal how to advance toward the remaining goals.
expectation: The inspection should identify an available partner for the next stage of the core's evolution.

effect: Silicon-burning material has no available partner on its own, so I need another route toward the goals.
reaction: That was surprising after the successive compression steps.
reason: The separate burning layers may need to be assembled into the star's layered interior; inspecting the star can check that route.
expectation: The inspection should reveal whether the star can combine with one of the available layers.

alternatives.reason: The layers might instead be assembled directly.

effect: The star also has no available partner, so the layers likely need to be combined independently.
reaction: It is surprising that neither the star nor the silicon-burning material has an available operation.
reason: Combining the carbon- and oxygen-burning layers is a plausible way to assemble the layered interior.
expectation: The two burning regions may form part of the layered stellar interior.

alternatives.reason: Inspection could identify its available partners before attempting assembly.

effect: Combining the burning layers built the layered interior, completing one goal.
reaction: The onion metaphor makes the coexistence of burning regions clear.
reason: The silicon-burning material moves nuclei toward the iron group, so combining it with the layered interior may advance the core to the end of fusion support.
expectation: The silicon-burning region should advance the layered star toward an iron-group core.

effect: The silicon-burning material and layered shells produced an iron-group core, completing the final goal and showing why further fusion cannot sustain the star.
reaction: The link between iron-group nuclei and the loss of fusion support was satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the onion of burning shells made the coexistence of different burning regions clear without implying they were separate stars or pure shells.

leastWorthwhile.text: Inspecting the star after silicon-burning material had no available partner was another unproductive check.

surprise.text: Silicon-burning material had no available partner until the other layers were assembled; I expected it to advance directly.

arbitrary.text: The need to combine the carbon- and oxygen-burning layers before the silicon material became usable was not initially obvious, though the resulting layered-interior explanation gave it a purpose.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the approaching core collapse unfolds, especially after learning why fusion support ends.
